sections.h2: Where is the Alpena County Register of Deeds and when can you record?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is at 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, in Alpena, and the phone number is 989-354-9547. The county's office page gives hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

The cutoffs for same-day recording are earlier than the doors-close time. E-recordings are accepted from 8 a.m. until 3:30 p.m. each day, and paper or walk-in documents until 4:00 p.m. Anything that arrives after those times is put on the next business day, so a Friday afternoon deed lands on Monday's record.

The office needs the original document, and it goes through indexing before it comes back to the sender, usually within a week of the recording date. Staff do not hand out blank deeds or help fill them in. The page points sellers to an office supply store, an attorney or a title company for that.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Alpena County?
sections.html:
Michigan sets a flat $30 fee for recording a document, no matter how many pages it runs, in MCL 600.2567. Only a charter county may set a different schedule by ordinance, so call the office if you want the total confirmed before you send funds.

  • $30 per recorded document, with $3 more for each extra instrument assigned or discharged by the same paper.
  • $1 per page for copies and $5 to certify a recorded document.
  • 50 cents for each year searched in a grantor or grantee index, with a $5 minimum.
  • A tax certification fee for some deed types. Ask the Alpena County treasurer which applies to yours.

The office page also links a fee sheet, a recording requirements sheet and e-recording instructions if you want the full list.

sections.h2: How can you search or copy Alpena County records?
sections.html:
The office offers two search tools, Laredo and Tapestry. Tapestry suits a one-time copy or two, while Laredo is aimed at title companies and people who search often.

The register also runs a free property fraud alert and a free notary fraud alert for Alpena County. Both send a phone, text or email message if a document with your name is recorded. An owner who is about to sell may want to sign up.

The office is also a certified passport agent and takes passport photos, so expect some of the foot traffic at the counter to be unrelated to land.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does the seller owe in Alpena County?
sections.html:
The seller owes $0.55 per $500 to the county under MCL 207.504 and $3.75 per $500 to the state under MCL 207.525. The Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied Alpena County home at $153,900 for 2020 to 2024.

Worked transfer tax for a $153,900 Alpena County sale (308 units of $500), from MCL 207.504 and 207.525
PartMathResult
County308 x $0.55$169.40
State308 x $3.75$1,155.00
Both308 x $4.30$1,324.40

The payment goes to the Alpena County treasurer, and the statute sets a 15 day window after the deed is delivered. If the property sells together with furniture or equipment, the tax applies only to the real property when the deed or an attached affidavit states the two values separately.

sections.h2: Which Alpena County transfers are exempt from transfer tax?
sections.html:
The state act lists exemptions in MCL 207.526. Three of them matter most to sellers in a distress or probate situation.

  • A deed given in foreclosure, or in lieu of foreclosure, on a mortgage. The exemption does not cover the lender's later sale of that property.
  • A transfer ordered by a court of record, unless the court sets a money price for it.
  • A land contract under which legal title stays with the seller until the full price is paid.
  • A conveyance that sets up or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spouses.

A seller who paid the tax and later finds an exemption applied can ask the Department of Treasury for a refund.

sections.h2: What paperwork details does Michigan require on an Alpena County deed?
sections.html:
MCL 565.201 lists what a register may check before accepting a paper. A short list of those items catches most problems.

  • Each signer's name printed under the signature, in black or dark blue ink, matching the notary's acknowledgment.
  • The notary's name printed on the same page near the signature.
  • The grantee's full address.
  • The name and business address of the drafter.
  • No more than the last 4 digits of a Social Security number.
  • An English translation attached if any part is in another language.

A register may not reject a compliant paper because of its content, so a clean format is the best protection against delay.

sections.h2: How should you time a deed for the Alpena County recording window?
sections.html:
Plan the signing so the deed reaches the register well before the afternoon cutoffs. A title company that e-records has until 3:30 p.m., which leaves half an hour less than a walk-in.

  • Confirm the grantee's mailing address is printed on the deed.
  • Print the notary's name beside the notary signature.
  • State the full sale value on the deed, or attach the value affidavit.
  • Send the original, because the office needs it for recording and returns it after indexing.
  • Check the county treasurer's requirements for any certification step.

If the sale falls on a Friday and the paperwork misses the cutoff, the record date moves to the following business day.

sections.h2: What is Alpena County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Alpena County sits on the northeast side of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, with Lake Huron and Thunder Bay along the east side and the Thunder Bay River draining most of the land. The state created it in 1840 as Anamickee County, renamed it Alpena in 1843, and organized it in 1857. The 45th parallel crosses the county, and Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary lies offshore.

Alpena is the only city and the county seat, Hillman is a village that lies partly in the county, and Alpena Charter Township and the Ossineke area round out the settled places. U.S. 23 follows the shoreline, M-32 ends in downtown Alpena, and M-65 gives a more direct way south than the shoreline highway.

The Census Bureau counts 28,853 residents in its 2025 estimate, a slight 0.2 percent drop from the 2020 base, with 27.9 percent aged 65 or more. Eighty percent of homes are owner occupied, median household income is $53,950, and the mean commute is 17.5 minutes. Median gross rent is $673.

Offshore, automated lighthouses stand on Middle Island and Thunder Bay Island, and the Mackinaw State Forest covers large tracts inland. The Census Bureau counts 822 employer establishments and 10,141 jobs in the county for 2023, and health care and social assistance receipts of about $389 million for 2022, and retail sales of about $616 million for 2022.

Assessments in Michigan are handled locally, so a seller with a question about a parcel should ask the city or township assessor, not the register of deeds.

faqs.q: What time does the Alpena County Register of Deeds stop taking recordings?
faqs.a: Paper and walk-in documents are accepted until 4:00 p.m., and e-recordings until 3:30 p.m. Later submissions go on the next business day's record.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Alpena County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The number is 989-354-9547, and the fax is 989-354-9646. The office is at 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, in Alpena.

faqs.q: Will Alpena County return my original deed after recording?
faqs.a: Yes, after the document is indexed. The office page says that usually happens within a week of the recording date.

faqs.q: How much is the Michigan state transfer tax on a $153,900 house?
faqs.a: It is $1,155.00 for the state share, from $3.75 on each $500 or fraction of $500. The county adds $169.40, so the two together are $1,324.40.

faqs.q: Can the Alpena County register give me a blank deed or advice?
faqs.a: No. The office cannot help complete documents or offer legal advice, and it does not supply blank deeds. Use a title company, an attorney or an office supply store.
